<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Open when final-writer rejection leaves a delivery claim RUNNING.

F270 R2 closed both original witnesses. Empty-sender ACK errors leave the claim
running and no new legacy wildcard; real sender's same id stays independent.
Scoped refused-control records preserve self's refusal across a parent's same-id
execution. Four mutants independently restored the failures or lost legacy replay.

ACK rejection is not a terminal policy. Ordinary/native Queue::claim has no
three-expiry lifetime budget: four forced expired leases left the bad row RUNNING,
attempt4, lease_expirations0. It blocks its serial key, not other recipients.
Explicit terminal ACK freed it. OMP/Pi extension leases have a different budget
and Working brake. No new normal producer path to a senderless row was found;
opaque generic/legacy rows still need diagnosis or quarantine (C34 follow-up).

Legacy match-any refusal is absent/null from, not every fallback. A fallback new
OWN-sender refusal can replay too; new OTHER-sender refusal cannot. New product
writers always include from, and the dedicated scoped record survives later
unscoped outcomes. The byte-length prefix avoids delimiter/UTF-8 key aliases.

Magic wand: final ACK atomicity, claim recovery/terminalization, other-key progress
and positive/negative replay identity should be independent queue-contract rows.
